name: Conservative Rasterization via Triangle Expansion
aliases: Conservative Rasterization via Geometry Shader Expansion
Conservative Rasterization via Triangle Expansion — Hole Repair via Conservative Rasterization, Triangle Expansion Method
definition: A technique to fix holes caused by standard rasterization (which only covers pixels whose centers are inside the triangle) by expanding the triangle in clip space and then culling the expanded area in the fragment shader.
summary: Conservative Rasterization via Triangle Expansion eliminates voxelization holes by manually expanding triangle boundaries in the geometry shader, avoiding hardware extensions or post-processing.
